functions.name: ZMusic_GetLastError
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the most recent error that occurred in the ZMusic library. Intended for diagnostic/logging after an API call fails.
requirements: Call only for diagnostics; returned pointer should be treated as read-only.
The lifetime/ownership of the returned string is unknown; copy it if you need to keep it.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetCallbacks
functions.description: Installs client-provided callbacks for messaging and optional soundfont virtualization/management. If message callbacks are not provided, messages go to stdout. If any of the soundfont management callbacks are set, all of them must be set.
requirements: callbacks may be NULL to clear callbacks (behavior beyond message routing is unknown).
If one of the soundfont management callbacks (OpenSoundFont, SF_OpenFile, SF_AddToSearchPath, SF_Close) is set, all must be set.
MessageFunc, if provided, must be callable at the severities defined by EZMusicMessageSeverity.
PathForSoundfont and NicePath are optional and may be NULL if not used.
All function pointers provided must remain valid while in use by the library.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetGenMidi
functions.description: Provides GenMIDI instrument data required for OPL playback. Without this, the OPL synth will not work.
requirements: data must point to a valid GenMIDI data block; size is unspecified in the API.
The pointer must remain valid at least until the library has consumed the data (exact ownership/lifetime is unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_SetWgOpn
functions.signature: void ZMusic_SetWgOpn(const void* data, unsigned len)
functions.description: Sets the default OPN bank data. Without this, OPN only works with custom banks.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
len must accurately describe the size of the provided bank data.
The buffer should remain valid until the library has consumed it (ownership semantics are unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_SetDmxGus
functions.signature: void ZMusic_SetDmxGus(const void* data, unsigned len)
functions.description: Provides DMXGUS data for running the GUS synth in actual GUS mode.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes containing DMXGUS data.
len must match the buffer size.
The buffer should remain valid until the library has consumed it (ownership semantics are unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_GetConfiguration
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a read-only array of configuration option descriptors. The array is terminated by an empty entry where all elements are 0.
requirements: Treat the returned array as read-only.
Iterate until an entry is encountered with all fields zeroed to detect the end.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: ZMusic_IdentifyMIDIType
functions.description: Heuristically identifies the MIDI file type from the given data buffer. Intended to support MIDI dumpers.
requirements: id must point to at least size bytes of readable memory containing the beginning of the MIDI data.
size must be >= 0; larger values may improve detection reliability.
The function does not take ownership of the buffer.

functions.name: ZMusic_CreateMIDISource
functions.signature: ZMusic_MidiSource ZMusic_CreateMIDISource(const uint8_t* data, size_t length, EMIDIType miditype)
functions.description: Creates an internal MIDI source handle from a memory buffer and an expected MIDI type. Used for further processing (e.g., dumping or rendering).
requirements: data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory containing the MIDI data.
length must correctly reflect the data size.
miditype should correspond to the data format (exact behavior if mismatched is unknown).
The returned handle must later be used only with ZMusic functions that accept ZMusic_MidiSource.

functions.name: ZMusic_MIDIDumpWave
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ZMusic_MIDIDumpWave(ZMusic_MidiSource source, EMidiDevice devtype, const char* devarg, const char* outname, int subsong, int samplerate)
functions.description: Renders the given MIDI source to a WAV file using the specified MIDI device backend and options. Intended to run on the client side for filesystem access.
requirements: source must be a valid handle returned by ZMusic_CreateMIDISource.
outname must be a valid, writable file path.
samplerate should be a positive integer.
devtype must be one of EMidiDevice values; devarg usage depends on the device (details unknown).
subsong selection semantics are device/data dependent (details unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_OpenSong
functions.signature: ZMusic_MusicStream ZMusic_OpenSong(ZMusicCustomReader* reader, EMidiDevice device, const char* Args)
functions.description: Opens a music stream from a custom reader using the specified MIDI device and optional argument string.
requirements: reader must point to a valid ZMusicCustomReader with all required function pointers populated for reading/seek/tell/close.
If reader is used for soundfonts or virtualized files, its callbacks must obey the ZMusicCustomReader contract (read/seek/tell return values consistent with stdio semantics).
device must be a valid EMidiDevice.
Args may be NULL or device-specific (details unknown).
The returned stream must be managed with ZMusic_Start/Stop/Close, etc.

functions.name: ZMusic_OpenSongFile
functions.signature: ZMusic_MusicStream ZMusic_OpenSongFile(const char* filename, EMidiDevice device, const char* Args)
functions.description: Opens a music stream from a file path using the specified MIDI device and optional argument string.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL path to a readable music file.
device must be a valid EMidiDevice.
Args may be NULL or device-specific (details unknown).
The returned stream must be closed with ZMusic_Close when no longer needed.

functions.name: ZMusic_OpenSongMem
functions.signature: ZMusic_MusicStream ZMusic_OpenSongMem(const void* mem, size_t size, EMidiDevice device, const char* Args)
functions.description: Opens a music stream from a memory buffer using the specified MIDI device and optional argument string.
requirements: mem must point to at least size bytes of readable memory containing the music data.
size must match the buffer length.
device must be a valid EMidiDevice.
Args may be NULL or device-specific (details unknown).
The returned stream must be closed with ZMusic_Close when finished.

functions.name: ZMusic_OpenCDSong
functions.description: Creates a music stream that plays audio from a CD track.
requirements: track should identify the CD track to play (exact valid range is unknown).
cdid selects the CD device (meaning is unknown).
The returned stream must be closed with ZMusic_Close.

functions.name: ZMusic_FillStream
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ZMusic_FillStream(ZMusic_MusicStream stream, void* buff, int len)
functions.description: Fills an audio buffer with decoded PCM data from the given music stream for pull-based streaming.
requirements: stream must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream opened by one of the ZMusic_Open* functions.
buff must point to writable memory of at least len bytes.
len must be a non-negative number of bytes to fill and should match the format/buffer size obtained via ZMusic_GetStreamInfo/Ex.
Call periodically while playing for streaming backends.

functions.name: ZMusic_Start
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ZMusic_Start(ZMusic_MusicStream song, int subsong, zmusic_bool loop)
functions.description: Starts playback of the given music stream at the specified subsong, with optional looping.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
subsong index semantics depend on the file (details unknown).
loop must be 0 or 1 (zmusic_bool).
Should be called before attempting to pull audio from a non-autostarting stream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Pause
functions.description: Pauses playback of the given music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream that is currently playing or paused.

functions.name: ZMusic_Resume
functions.description: Resumes playback of a paused music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream previously paused with ZMusic_Pause.

functions.name: ZMusic_Update
functions.description: Performs periodic maintenance/update on the given music stream. Some backends may require this to progress playback/state.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
Should be called periodically if the backend requires updates (exact cadence unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_IsPlaying
functions.description: Returns whether the given music stream is currently playing.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Stop
functions.description: Stops playback of the given music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Close
functions.description: Closes and releases resources associated with a music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream that has not already been closed.
After this call, the stream handle must not be used again.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetSubsong
functions.description: Selects a different subsong for the given music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
subsong must be a valid index for the current content (valid range unknown).

functions.name: ZMusic_IsLooping
functions.description: Returns whether the given music stream is configured to loop.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetDeviceType
functions.description: Returns the device type used by the stream, likely corresponding to EMidiDevice values.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
Interpretation of the returned int is library-specific (likely EMidiDevice).

functions.name: ZMusic_IsMIDI
functions.description: Returns whether the given music stream is a MIDI-based source.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_VolumeChanged
functions.description: Notifies the stream that external volume settings changed so it can update its internal state.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_WriteSMF
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ZMusic_WriteSMF(ZMusic_MidiSource source, const char* fn, int looplimit)
functions.description: Writes the given MIDI source to a Standard MIDI File (SMF) at the specified path, with an optional loop limit.
requirements: source must be a valid ZMusic_MidiSource.
fn must be a valid, writable file path.
looplimit semantics and valid range are unknown; non-negative values are typical for limits.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetStreamInfo
functions.description: Retrieves basic stream parameters such as buffer size, sample rate, and channel count. If mBufferSize is 0, the song does not use streaming. If mNumChannels is negative, 16-bit integer format is used instead of floating point.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
info must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable SoundStreamInfo struct.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetStreamInfoEx
functions.description: Retrieves extended stream parameters: buffer size, sample rate, sample type (UInt8/Int16/Float32), and channel config (Mono/Stereo). If mBufferSize is 0, the song does not use streaming.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
info must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable SoundStreamInfoEx struct.

functions.name: ChangeMusicSettingInt
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ChangeMusicSettingInt(EIntConfigKey key, ZMusic_MusicStream song, int value, int* pRealValue)
functions.description: Changes an integer music configuration setting. Returns whether a music restart is needed. The value actually applied may be written back via pRealValue.
requirements: key must be a valid EIntConfigKey.
song may be a specific stream or global target depending on key (details unknown).
pRealValue may be NULL if the caller does not need the applied value.
Check the boolean return value to determine if a restart is needed.

functions.name: ChangeMusicSettingFloat
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ChangeMusicSettingFloat(EFloatConfigKey key, ZMusic_MusicStream song, float value, float* pRealValue)
functions.description: Changes a floating-point music configuration setting. Returns whether a music restart is needed. The applied value may be written back via pRealValue.
requirements: key must be a valid EFloatConfigKey.
song may be a specific stream or global target depending on key (details unknown).
pRealValue may be NULL if the caller does not need the applied value.
Check the boolean return value to determine if a restart is needed.

functions.name: ChangeMusicSettingString
functions.signature: zmusic_bool ChangeMusicSettingString(EStringConfigKey key, ZMusic_MusicStream song, const char* value)
functions.description: Changes a string music configuration setting. Returns whether a music restart is needed.
requirements: key must be a valid EStringConfigKey.
song may be a specific stream or global target depending on key (details unknown).
value must be a valid, null-terminated string appropriate for the setting.
Check the boolean return value to determine if a restart is needed.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetStats
functions.description: Returns a textual statistics string for the given music stream.
requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
Treat the returned string as read-only; lifetime is unknown—copy if you need to persist it.

functions.name: CreateDecoder
functions.signature: struct SoundDecoder* CreateDecoder(const uint8_t* data, size_t size, zmusic_bool isstatic)
functions.description: Creates a generic audio decoder for the given memory buffer. Useful for non-stream music decoding tasks.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory containing the audio data.
size must match the buffer length.
If isstatic is true, the data buffer may need to remain valid for the lifetime of the decoder (exact requirement inferred by name; details unknown).
The returned decoder must be managed with SoundDecoder_* functions.

functions.name: SoundDecoder_GetInfo
functions.signature: void SoundDecoder_GetInfo(struct SoundDecoder* decoder, int* samplerate, ChannelConfig* chans, SampleType* type)
functions.description: Retrieves audio properties (sample rate, channel configuration, sample type) from a decoder.
requirements: decoder must be a valid pointer returned by CreateDecoder.
samplerate, chans, and type must be non-NULL pointers to writable outputs.

functions.name: SoundDecoder_Read
functions.signature: size_t SoundDecoder_Read(struct SoundDecoder* decoder, void* buffer, size_t length)
functions.description: Decodes up to length bytes of PCM data from the decoder into buffer. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: decoder must be a valid pointer returned by CreateDecoder.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least length bytes.
length must be the maximum number of bytes to read; the function may return fewer.

functions.name: SoundDecoder_Close
functions.description: Closes and frees resources associated with a SoundDecoder.
requirements: decoder must be a valid decoder pointer obtained from CreateDecoder.
After this call, the decoder pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: FindLoopTags
functions.signature: void FindLoopTags(const uint8_t* data, size_t size, uint32_t* start, zmusic_bool* startass, uint32_t* end, zmusic_bool* endass)
functions.description: Scans the provided data buffer for loop metadata and outputs discovered loop start/end positions and whether each was auto-assigned/assumed.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
start, startass, end, and endass must be valid pointers if you expect corresponding outputs; any may be NULL if you do not need that output (behavior for NULL is inferred; not explicitly documented).
size must match the buffer length.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetMidiDevices
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an array of available MIDI output devices and writes the number of devices to pAmount.
requirements: pAmount must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of devices.
Treat the returned array as read-only; ownership and lifetime are not specified—do not free it.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetADLBanks
functions.description: Retrieves available ADL bank names. Returns the number of banks and outputs a pointer to an array of C strings via pNames.
requirements: pNames must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the array pointer.
The returned names and array are read-only; do not free them.
Use the returned count to index the names array.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for GenMIDI (Doom-format) instrument data.
# Reference characteristics:
# - Header: ASCII "#OPL_II#" (8 bytes)
# - Then 175 instrument entries (per Doom): 128 melodic + 47 percussion
# - Each instrument entry is 36 bytes when including 2 operators and metadata in Doom's GENMIDI.
#   However, many engines accept a variety of flavors as long as header matches and there is at
#   least one well-formed instrument. Some readers accept minimal tables as long as size matches
#   expectations. Because the fuzz stub only passes a pointer and size is unknown to callee, we
#   produce a full table to maximize validity across implementations.
#
# We will generate a valid looking table:
# - Header "#OPL_II#"
# - Followed by instrument count (we include full table of 175 entries)
# - For each instrument we create plausible OPL operator parameters within legal ranges.
# - Some engines expect Doom layout of 175 instruments * 36 bytes after header without explicit
#   count. To be broadly compatible, we write exactly 175 entries and no explicit count field.
#   The classic Doom GENMIDI layout after the header is just the 175 instrument records.
#
# Instrument record layout (Doom GENMIDI): 36 bytes
# Byte order per instrument (per various docs):
#   For each of 2 operators (modulator, carrier):
#     0: trem/vibr/sustain/kbd scale (0-255 bitfield)
#     1: ksl/volume (0-255 bitfield)
#     2: attack/decay (0-255 bitfield)
#     3: sustain/release (0-255 bitfield)
#     4: waveform select (0-7)
#     5: feedback/connection for modulator or unused for carrier in some variants (0-255)
#   Then:
#     2 bytes: base note/finetune (or unused), 2 bytes: percussion mapping (varies)
#     2 bytes: transpose, 2 bytes: finetune
#     Remaining pad to 36 bytes.
# Different ports vary; readers typically mask bits and won’t crash if within byte ranges.
# Here we ensure sane ranges and fixed 36 bytes per instrument.

HEADER = b"#OPL_II#"
INSTRUMENTS = 175
RECORD_SIZE = 36
MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_bits(r: random.Random, mask: int, base: int = 0) -> int:
    return (r.randint(0, 255) & mask) | base


def _op_params(r: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Generate plausible OPL operator parameters.
    tvsk = _rand_bits(r, 0xFF)  # trem/vib/sus/ksr
    ksl_vol = ((r.randrange(0, 4) << 6) | r.randrange(0, 64))  # ksl 0-3, vol 0-63
    attack_decay = ((r.randrange(0, 16) << 4) | r.randrange(0, 16))
    sustain_release = ((r.randrange(0, 16) << 4) | r.randrange(0, 16))
    wave = r.randrange(0, 8)
    return [tvsk, ksl_vol, attack_decay, sustain_release, wave]


def _instrument_record(r: random.Random, percussion: bool) -> bytes:
    # Two operators: modulator then carrier
    mod = _op_params(r)
    car = _op_params(r)
    # Feedback/connection byte: 0-7 for feedback in lower 3 bits; bit 0 of connection varies.
    fb_conn = (r.randrange(0, 8) | (r.randrange(0, 2) << 7))

    data = bytearray()
    # Modulator block (5 bytes) + feedback byte
    data.extend(bytes(mod))
    data.append(fb_conn)
    # Carrier block (5 bytes) + dummy byte to align like many implementations
    data.extend(bytes(car))
    data.append(0)

    # Pitch/transpose/finetune like fields; fill with reasonable defaults
    base_note = 60 if not percussion else 35  # middle C or kick
    finetune = r.randrange(-32, 33) & 0xFF
    transpose = r.randrange(-12, 13) & 0xFF

    # 2 bytes base note/unused, 2 bytes percussion key if percussion, else zeros
    data.append(base_note & 0xFF)
    data.append(0)
    if percussion:
        perc_key = r.choice([35, 36, 38, 40, 41, 42, 43, 45, 47, 49, 51])
        data.append(perc_key & 0xFF)
        data.append(0)
    else:
        data.append(0)
        data.append(0)

    # transpose, finetune (2 bytes each)
    data.append(transpose)
    data.append(0)
    data.append(finetune)
    data.append(0)

    # Pad to RECORD_SIZE with zeros
    if len(data) < RECORD_SIZE:
        data.extend(b"\x00" * (RECORD_SIZE - len(data)))
    else:
        data[:] = data[:RECORD_SIZE]
    return bytes(data)


def _build_genmidi(r: random.Random, full: bool = True) -> bytes:
    buf = bytearray()
    buf.extend(HEADER)

    count = INSTRUMENTS if full else r.randrange(32, INSTRUMENTS + 1)

    # Doom layout is exactly 175 instruments after header. For non-full, we still pad
    # to at least a minimal plausible size while staying under 4096 bytes.

    # First 128 melodic
    melodic = min(128, count)
    for _ in range(melodic):
        buf.extend(_instrument_record(r, percussion=False))

    # Remaining percussion up to 47
    remaining = max(0, count - melodic)
    perc = min(47, remaining)
    for _ in range(perc):
        buf.extend(_instrument_record(r, percussion=True))

    # If we generated fewer than 175 for variety, some readers still expect full table.
    # Optionally pad with zeros or additional generic instruments to reach a boundary.
    if full:
        pass
    else:
        # Pad to next multiple of RECORD_SIZE to avoid truncated last record.
        rem = len(buf) % RECORD_SIZE
        if rem != 0:
            pad = RECORD_SIZE - rem
            buf.extend(b"\x00" * pad)

    # Size guard
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_SIZE])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose between full canonical table and shorter valid table
    full = r.random() < 0.7

    gen = _build_genmidi(r, full=full)

    # Occasionally vary header case (some loaders are strict; keep default mostly)
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        mutable = bytearray(gen)
        # Keep exact 8 bytes but vary last two to a known alt seen in some ports (still valid-ish)
        mutable[6] = ord('_')  # keep as underscore
        mutable[7] = ord('#')
        gen = bytes(mutable)

    return gen

import random
import io

# Generator for Yamaha OPN bank data (WOPN-like). We craft a small but valid
# bank with a header, one bank with a handful of patches, and deterministic
# randomness from the provided seed. The layout is designed to be accepted by
# typical WOPN readers:
# - Magic: b"WOPN"
# - Version: uint32 (e.g., 0x00010000)
# - Bank count: uint32
# - Reserved: 8 bytes
# - For each bank:
#   - Name: 32-byte ASCII, NUL-padded
#   - Patch count: uint32
#   - For each patch (operator parameters loosely modeled after OPN/OPM style):
#       - Patch name: 32-byte ASCII, NUL-padded
#       - Algorithm: uint8 (0..7)
#       - Feedback: uint8 (0..7)
#       - LFO enable: uint8 (0/1)
#       - LFO rate: uint8 (0..127)
#       - PitchEG: uint8
#       - AmpModSens: uint8
#       - KeySync: uint8
#       - Detune: int8
#       - PitchModDepth: uint8
#       - Reserved: 6 bytes (zero)
#       - For 4 operators (op1..op4):
#           - AR, DR, SR, RR: uint8 (0..31)
#           - SL: uint8 (0..15)
#           - TL: uint8 (0..127)
#           - KS: uint8 (0..3)
#           - MUL: uint8 (0..15)
#           - DT2: uint8 (0..3)
#           - AMS-EN: uint8 (0/1)
#           - SSGEG: uint8 (0..15)
# This is not the canonical spec, but follows common expectations seen in
# various WOPN consumers and remains internally consistent.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _padded_ascii(s: str, length: int) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:length]
    return b + b'\x00' * (length - len(b))

class R:
    def __init__(self, seed: int):
        self.r = random.Random(seed)
    def randint(self, a, b):
        return self.r.randint(a, b)
    def choice(self, seq):
        return self.r.choice(seq)
    def randname(self, prefix: str, maxlen: int) -> str:
        base = prefix + '_' + ''.join(self.choice('ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789') for _ in range(self.randint(3, maxlen- len(prefix) - 1)))
        return base[:maxlen]


def _pack_patch(rng: R, patch_index: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a single patch with sensible ranges
    name = _padded_ascii(rng.randname(f"Patch{patch_index}", 16), 32)
    alg = rng.randint(0, 7)
    fb = rng.randint(0, 7)
    lfo_en = rng.randint(0, 1)
    lfo_rate = rng.randint(0, 127)
    pitcheg = rng.randint(0, 1)
    ams = rng.randint(0, 3)
    keysync = rng.randint(0, 1)
    detune = rng.randint(-7, 7) & 0xFF  # store as int8 via byte value
    pmd = rng.randint(0, 127)
    reserved = b"\x00" * 6

    hdr = name + bytes([alg, fb, lfo_en, lfo_rate, pitcheg, ams, keysync, detune, pmd]) + reserved

    def op_params():
        AR = rng.randint(0, 31)
        DR = rng.randint(0, 31)
        SR = rng.randint(0, 31)
        RR = rng.randint(0, 31)
        SL = rng.randint(0, 15)
        TL = rng.randint(0, 127)
        KS = rng.randint(0, 3)
        MUL = rng.randint(0, 15)
        DT2 = rng.randint(0, 3)
        AMSEN = rng.randint(0, 1)
        SSGEG = rng.randint(0, 15)
        return bytes([AR, DR, SR, RR, SL, TL, KS, MUL, DT2, AMSEN, SSGEG])

    ops = b"".join(op_params() for _ in range(4))
    return hdr + ops


def _pack_bank(rng: R, bank_index: int, patch_count: int) -> bytes:
    bank_name = _padded_ascii(rng.randname(f"Bank{bank_index}", 16), 32)
    out = io.BytesIO()
    out.write(bank_name)
    out.write(struct.pack('<I', patch_count))
    for i in range(patch_count):
        out.write(_pack_patch(rng, i))
    return out.getvalue()


def _build_wopn(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = R(seed)
    # Decide number of banks and patches per bank within reasonable limits
    bank_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    patches_per_bank = [rng.randint(4, 16) for _ in range(bank_count)]

    header = io.BytesIO()
    header.write(b"WOPN")
    header.write(struct.pack('<I', 0x00010000))  # version 1.0.0.0
    header.write(struct.pack('<I', bank_count))
    header.write(b"\x00" * 8)  # reserved

    body = io.BytesIO()
    for bidx, pcount in enumerate(patches_per_bank):
        body.write(_pack_bank(rng, bidx, pcount))

    blob = header.getvalue() + body.getvalue()
    # Ensure size cap
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a valid OPN bank blob suitable for ZMusic_SetWgOpn(data, len)
    data = _build_wopn(seed)
    # Guarantee non-empty and minimally sized content
    if not data:
        return b"WOPN\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00"*8
    return data

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# DMXGUS configuration data generator
# Goal: produce valid-looking DMXGUS blobs that ZMusic_SetDmxGus can consume.
# The format is not fully specified here, but historically DMXGUS lumps are
# ASCII text with INSTRUMENT/PATCH mapping lines, comments, and optional headers.
# We'll create plausible text-based configurations covering a variety of features:
# - Header/comment lines (e.g., #, ;)
# - DEVICE/GUS specific directives often seen in DMXGUS configs
# - PATCH/INSTR/DRUM mappings, multiple banks, ranges, pan/volume, envelopes
# - Whitespace variations and mixed line endings
# - Optional binary padding/trailer to emulate embedded resource blobs
# - Ensure non-empty output and length <= 4096

_ASCII_WORDS = [
    "GUS", "ULTRASND", "MIDI", "PATCH", "BANK", "VOICE", "STEREO",
    "REVERB", "CHORUS", "PAN", "VOLUME", "ENV", "ATTACK", "DECAY",
    "SUSTAIN", "RELEASE", "LOOP", "RANGE", "PROGRAM", "INSTR", "DRUM",
    "PERcussion", "TIMBRE", "MAP", "DMX", "DOOM", "HERETIC", "HEXEN",
]

_DEVICE_LINES = [
    "# DMXGUS configuration file",
    "; Generated by fuzz seed generator",
    "DEVICE GUS",
    "CARD ULTRASOUND",
    "PORT 0x240",
    "IRQ 5",
    "DMA 1 5",
]

# Example mapping line patterns commonly seen in old DMXGUS/DEMU config styles.
# These are not strict specifications; they generate reasonable mappings.

def _mk_patch_line(r: random.Random, program: int, bank: int = 0) -> str:
    # 0..127 program, bank 0..127
    name = r.choice([
        "PIANO", "EPiano", "Organ", "Guitar", "Bass", "Strings", "Brass",
        "Lead", "Pad", "Bell", "Perc", "Choir", "DrumKit", "Flute",
    ])
    pan = r.choice(["L", "R", "C"]) if r.random() < 0.5 else str(r.randint(0, 127))
    vol = r.randint(60, 127)
    # Some formats use: PATCH <bank> <program> <name> <pan> <vol>
    return f"PATCH {bank:02d} {program:03d} {name} {pan} {vol}"


def _mk_instr_line(r: random.Random, program: int, bank: int = 0) -> str:
    # Alternative mapping keyword
    wave = r.choice(["piano.pat", "guitar.pat", "bass.pat", "flute.pat", "lead.pat"]) 
    env = f"ENV {r.randint(0,127)},{r.randint(0,127)},{r.randint(0,127)},{r.randint(0,127)}"
    return f"INSTR {bank} {program} {wave} {env}"


def _mk_drum_line(r: random.Random, key: int) -> str:
    # GM drum keys 35..81
    wave = r.choice(["kick.pat", "snare.pat", "tom.pat", "hh.pat", "ride.pat", "perc.pat"]) 
    pan = r.randint(0, 127)
    vol = r.randint(50, 127)
    return f"DRUM {key:03d} {wave} PAN {pan} VOL {vol}"


def _mk_bank_header(r: random.Random, bank: int) -> str:
    return f"BANK {bank} ; bank definition"


def _mk_range_line(r: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int, program: int) -> str:
    lo = max(0, min(127, lo))
    hi = max(lo, min(127, hi))
    return f"RANGE {lo:03d}-{hi:03d} -> {program:03d}"


def _mk_comment(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = r.choice(["#", ";"])
    word = r.choice(_ASCII_WORDS)
    return f"{prefix} {word} setting"


def _mk_misc_directive(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # A few plausible misc directives seen in similar configs
    return r.choice([
        f"VOICES {r.randint(14, 32)}",
        f"STEREO {r.choice([0,1])}",
        f"REVERB {r.randint(0, 3)}",
        f"CHORUS {r.randint(0, 3)}",
        f"MASTER_VOL {r.randint(80,127)}",
        f"DEFAULT_PAN {r.randint(0,127)}",
    ])


def _line_ending(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(["\n", "\r\n", "\r"]) if r.random() < 0.7 else "\n"


def _build_text_section(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Header/device lines
    for ln in _DEVICE_LINES:
        if r.random() < 0.85:
            lines.append(ln)
    # Some comments and directives
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        lines.append(_mk_comment(r))
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        lines.append(_mk_misc_directive(r))

    # Banks and mappings
    bank_count = r.randint(1, 3)
    used_programs = set()
    for b in range(bank_count):
        if r.random() < 0.8:
            lines.append(_mk_bank_header(r, b))
        # A mix of INSTR/PATCH lines
        for _ in range(r.randint(6, 18)):
            p = r.randint(0, 127)
            used_programs.add((b, p))
            if r.random() < 0.55:
                lines.append(_mk_patch_line(r, p, b))
            else:
                lines.append(_mk_instr_line(r, p, b))
        # Optional ranges
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
                lo = r.randint(0, 120)
                hi = lo + r.randint(0, 7)
                prog = r.randint(0, 127)
                lines.append(_mk_range_line(r, lo, hi, prog))

    # Drum section
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        lines.append("; Drum mappings")
        for _ in range(r.randint(4, 16)):
            key = r.randint(35, 81)
            lines.append(_mk_drum_line(r, key))

    # Footer comments
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        lines.append(_mk_comment(r))

    # Join with mixed line endings
    eol = _line_ending(r)
    return eol.join(lines) + eol


def _maybe_binary_tail(r: random.Random, max_tail: int) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally append a small binary tail to emulate resource packing
    if r.random() < 0.35 and max_tail > 0:
        n = r.randint(4, min(64, max_tail))
        # Make it look like a small TLV-ish blob sometimes
        if r.random() < 0.5 and n >= 8:
            tag = r.choice([b"LOOP", b"GUS\x00", b"DMX\x01", b"CONF"])  # 4 bytes
            rem = n - 4
            payload = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rem))
            return tag + payload
        return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
    return b""


def _truncate_to_limit(data: bytes, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if len(data) <= limit:
        return data
    # Keep the header part more, trim tail
    return data[:limit]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a plausible text configuration section
    text = _build_text_section(r)
    data = text.encode('ascii', errors='replace')

    # Optional binary tail to vary buffers while keeping leading text valid
    tail_room = 4096 - len(data)
    if tail_room < 0:
        data = _truncate_to_limit(data)
        tail_room = 0
    tail = _maybe_binary_tail(r, tail_room)
    blob = data + tail

    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not blob:
        blob = b"; DMXGUS minimal\nPATCH 00 000 PIANO C 100\n"
    return _truncate_to_limit(blob)

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator focuses on producing valid MIDI-family data buffers that the target
# functions accept:
# - ZMusic_CreateMIDISource(const uint8_t* data, size_t length, EMIDIType miditype)
# - ZMusic_IdentifyMIDIType(uint32_t* id, int size)
#
# We generate small but valid examples for several formats:
# - Standard MIDI File (SMF) type 0 or 1 (header MThd + one or more MTrk chunks)
# - MUS (id "MUS\x1A") minimal playable stream with an end event
# - HMI (id "HMI-MIDISONG061595") header with at least one dummy track chunk
# - XMI (RIFF/RMID form with XMID LIST) minimal structure
# - MIDS (simple header signature "MIDS") minimal skeleton
#
# Buffers are kept <= 4096 bytes.

# Utility: write variable-length quantity used in MIDI delta-times

def _vlq(value: int) -> bytes:
    value = max(0, int(value))
    bytes_rev = []
    bytes_rev.append(value & 0x7F)
    value >>= 7
    while value:
        bytes_rev.append((value & 0x7F) | 0x80)
        value >>= 7
    return bytes(bytearray(reversed(bytes_rev)))

# Utility: MIDI running status-safe events (we include status each time for simplicity)

def _midi_note_on(ch: int, note: int, vel: int) -> bytes:
    ch &= 0x0F
    note = max(0, min(127, note))
    vel = max(0, min(127, vel))
    return bytes([0x90 | ch, note, vel])

def _midi_note_off(ch: int, note: int, vel: int=64) -> bytes:
    ch &= 0x0F
    note = max(0, min(127, note))
    vel = max(0, min(127, vel))
    return bytes([0x80 | ch, note, vel])

def _midi_program_change(ch: int, prog: int) -> bytes:
    ch &= 0x0F
    prog = max(0, min(127, prog))
    return bytes([0xC0 | ch, prog])

# Meta events

def _meta_event(type_byte: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0xFF, type_byte]) + _vlq(len(data)) + data

# Assemble a single MTrk with some deterministic but varied content

def _make_mtrk(rng: random.Random, ticks_per_quarter: int) -> bytes:
    events = bytearray()
    # Tempo meta 120 BPM (500000 us/qn)
    events += _vlq(0) + _meta_event(0x51, b"\x07\xA1\x20")
    # Time signature 4/4
    events += _vlq(0) + _meta_event(0x58, bytes([4, 2, 24, 8]))
    # Key signature C major
    events += _vlq(0) + _meta_event(0x59, bytes([0, 0]))
    # Program changes on a couple channels
    for ch in range(2):
        events += _vlq(0) + _midi_program_change(ch, rng.randint(0, 127))
    # A short scale phrase
    base = rng.choice([60, 62, 64, 65, 67])  # C/D/E/F/G
    length_ticks = max(30, ticks_per_quarter // 8)
    for i in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        note = base + i
        ch = rng.randint(0, 1)
        vel = rng.randint(40, 100)
        events += _vlq(rng.randint(0, 10)) + _midi_note_on(ch, note, vel)
        events += _vlq(length_ticks) + _midi_note_off(ch, note, 64)
    # End of track
    events += _vlq(0) + _meta_event(0x2F, b"")
    # Wrap with MTrk header
    body = bytes(events)
    return b"MTrk" + struct.pack(">I", len(body)) + body

# Build a valid SMF (Standard MIDI File)

def _build_smf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    format_type = rng.choice([0, 1])
    ntrks = 1 if format_type == 0 else rng.randint(1, 2)
    division = rng.choice([480, 240, 960, 96])
    mthd = b"MThd" + struct.pack(">IHHH", 6, format_type, ntrks, division)
    tracks = b"".join(_make_mtrk(rng, division) for _ in range(ntrks))
    return mthd + tracks

# Minimal MUS file (DOOM MUS). We include header and an immediate end event.
# Reference: header "MUS\x1A" followed by fields; events are compact. We'll place a few notes.

def _build_mus(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Header (size 16 bytes + 6 reserved = 24, but different variants exist). We'll follow common layout:
    # 0: id "MUS\x1A"
    # 4: score length (u16)
    # 6: score start (u16) offset from start of header
    # 8: channels (u16)
    # 10: sec_channels (u16)
    # 12: instr_cnt (u16)
    # 14: dummy/flags (u16)
    # 16..: instrument list (instr_cnt * u16)
    # After header+instruments, score data begins.
    events = bytearray()
    # Simple: set channel volume or play a note, then end.
    # MUS event format: [event | channelbits] ... We'll use simplest: release note and end.
    # We'll generate: a note on (code 0), then delta, note off, then end (code 6 with last flag)
    # Encoding helper per spec: event byte: (event_type << 4) | channel | lastflag<<7
    def mus_event(event_type: int, channel: int, last: int) -> int:
        return ((last & 1) << 7) | ((event_type & 0x7) << 4) | (channel & 0x0F)
    # Note on (type 0), with key and volume present
    ch = rng.randint(0, 8)
    key = rng.randint(48, 72)
    vol = rng.randint(40, 100)
    events += bytes([mus_event(0, ch, 0), key | 0x80, vol])
    # Small delta-time: variable-length, 7 bits per byte, high bit indicates continuation; use single 0 meaning 0 delta
    # Wait some time (e.g., 10)
    wait = 10
    # encode wait
    w = wait
    enc = []
    enc.append(w & 0x7F)
    events += bytes(enc)
    # Note off (type 1)
    events += bytes([mus_event(1, ch, 0), key])
    # End (type 6) with last flag set
    events += bytes([mus_event(6, 0, 1)])

    header_size = 16
    score_start = header_size  # instruments count = 0 so score follows immediately
    channels = 9
    sec_channels = 0
    instr_cnt = 0
    dummy = 0
    score_len = len(events)
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"MUS\x1A"
    header += struct.pack("<HHHHHH", score_len, score_start, channels, sec_channels, instr_cnt, dummy)
    return bytes(header) + bytes(events)

# Minimal HMI: signature at start and very simple structure. Different variants exist; we craft a plausible header
# with at least one track. Some engines just check the magic.

def _build_hmi(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Common HMI signature: "HMI-MIDISONG061595" at offset 0
    sig = b"HMI-MIDISONG061595\x00"
    # Followed by a simple chunked layout. We'll add minimal placeholders.
    # We'll include a track marker "HMI-" track with length and a tiny payload.
    track = b"HMI-" + struct.pack("<I", 4) + b"\x00\xFF\x2F\x00"  # end of track-like bytes
    # Compose header with pointers to track; keep lengths consistent.
    body = sig + track
    return body

# Minimal XMI inside RIFF RMID container: RIFF chunk with 'RMID' and 'data' containing a simple MIDI stream.

def _build_xmi(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # We'll wrap a tiny SMF chunk as data; some identifiers look for RIFF/RMID
    midi = _build_smf(rng)
    data_chunk = b"data" + struct.pack("<I", len(midi)) + midi
    riff_size = 4 + len(data_chunk)
    riff = b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", riff_size) + b"RMID" + data_chunk
    return riff

# Minimal MIDS format: Some games use "MIDS" magic plus a simple header. We'll craft a tiny stub.

def _build_mids(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Magic + version + length + one track of bytes
    payload = b"\x00\xFF\x2F\x00"  # resembles MIDI end marker bytes
    header = b"MIDS" + struct.pack("<II", 1, len(payload))
    return header + payload

# Pool of builders mapped loosely to EMIDIType enumeration order described in objects:
# EMIDIType: 0 NOTMIDI, 1 MIDI, 2 HMI, 3 XMI, 4 MUS, 5 MIDS

_BUILDERS = {
    1: _build_smf,
    2: _build_hmi,
    3: _build_xmi,
    4: _build_mus,
    5: _build_mids,
}

# Fallback: generic small SMF always valid

def _fallback_valid(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return _build_smf(rng)

# Optionally add interesting variants within SMF: type 0 vs 1, different divisions and meta content
# Already covered via random choices.


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target format biased toward valid identification: prefer MIDI/XMI/MUS too
    typ = rng.choices(population=[1, 4, 3, 2, 5], weights=[40, 20, 15, 15, 10], k=1)[0]
    builder = _BUILDERS.get(typ, _fallback_valid)
    data = builder(rng)
    # Ensure size limits
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Truncate safely only for container formats where trailing cut is okay; otherwise rebuild smaller SMF
        data = _fallback_valid(rng)
        if len(data) > 4096:
            data = data[:4096]
    # As a small variation, sometimes prepend or append harmless padding in container-accepted formats is NOT valid;
    # so we avoid adding padding to keep validity high.
    return bytes(data)

def _build_smf_midi(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal valid SMF with a single empty track and tempo/meta events.
    # Header chunk: 'MThd' 6 bytes, format 0/1, ntrks=1, division=480
    fmt = rng.choice([0, 1])
    division = rng.choice([96, 120, 192, 240, 480])
    header = b"MThd" + struct.pack(
        ">IHHH", 6, fmt, 1, division
    )
    # Track chunk with simple events: set tempo, time signature, end of track
    def vlq(n: int) -> bytes:
        # Encode variable-length quantity.
        bytes_rev = []
        bytes_rev.append(n & 0x7F)
        n >>= 7
        while n:
            bytes_rev.append(0x80 | (n & 0x7F))
            n >>= 7
        return bytes(bytearray(reversed(bytes_rev)))

    track_events = bytearray()
    # Delta 0, meta tempo (500000 us/qn = 120 BPM)
    track_events += vlq(0) + b"\xFF\x51\x03" + struct.pack(">I", 500000)[1:]
    # Delta 0, meta time signature 4/4
    track_events += vlq(0) + b"\xFF\x58\x04\x04\x02\x18\x08"
    # Program change on channel 0 to Acoustic Grand (0)
    track_events += vlq(rng.randint(0, 10)) + bytes([0xC0, rng.randint(0, 127)])
    # Note on C4, short duration
    vel = rng.randint(40, 100)
    track_events += vlq(0) + bytes([0x90, 60, vel])
    track_events += vlq(rng.randint(30, 120)) + bytes([0x80, 60, 64])
    # End of track
    track_events += vlq(0) + b"\xFF\x2F\x00"

    trk = b"MTrk" + struct.pack(">I", len(track_events)) + bytes(track_events)
    data = header + trk
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def _build_mus(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal valid MUS header with no events (for identification).
    # MUS header from Doom: "MUS\x1A" then 16-bit little endian fields.
    # We'll provide a tiny score length/offset and a short channel count.
    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr += b"MUS\x1A"
    def le16(v):
        return struct.pack("<H", v)
    def le32(v):
        return struct.pack("<I", v)
    # Header fields per MUS format:
    # 0x04: scoreLen (LE16), 0x06: scoreStart (LE16), 0x08: channels (LE16)
    # 0x0A: secChannels (LE16), 0x0C: instrCnt (LE16), 0x0E: dummy (LE16), 0x10: ofsinstr (LE32)
    score = b"\x00"  # minimal end marker would be 0x00 with last=1; here just stub
    scoreLen = len(score)
    scoreStart = 0x14  # right after header
    hdr += le16(scoreLen)
    hdr += le16(scoreStart)
    hdr += le16(4)     # channels
    hdr += le16(0)     # sec channels
    hdr += le16(0)     # instrument count
    hdr += le16(0)     # dummy
    hdr += le32(0)     # ofsinstr
    data = bytes(hdr) + score
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def _build_hmi(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Very small HMI header stub. Many implementations look for signature.
    # Put signature and some plausible header bytes.

    sig = b"HMI-MIDISONG\x00"
    body = bytearray(sig)
    body += b"\x00" * 32
    return bytes(body[:MAX_SIZE])


def _build_xmi(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # XMI is RIFF-like with FORM/XDIR or XMID chunks. Provide minimal FORM XMID.

    content = b"XMID" + b"CAT " + struct.pack(">I", 0) + b"INFO"
    size = len(content)
    data = b"FORM" + struct.pack(">I", size) + content
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

# Minimal but valid MIDI file generator (SMF Type 0 or 1 with a short track)
# This aims to produce inputs that ZMusic_OpenSongFile and write/dump paths can consume.
# The framework will ensure the filename points to a fuzz-data file; our buffer is used
# to seed that file's content.

def _u32be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(n >> 24) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, n & 0xFF])


def _u16be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(n >> 8) & 0xFF, n & 0xFF])


def _varlen(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Encode MIDI variable-length quantity
    buf = n & 0x7F
    out = [buf]
    n >>= 7
    while n > 0:
        out.insert(0, (n & 0x7F) | 0x80)
        n >>= 7
    return bytes(out)


def _make_simple_smf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose Type 0 or Type 1 for broader coverage
    fmt = 0 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 1
    ntrks = 1 if fmt == 0 else rng.randint(1, 2)
    division = rng.choice([480, 960, 192, 1000])
    header = b"MThd" + _u32be(6) + _u16be(fmt) + _u16be(ntrks) + _u16be(division)

    def make_track() -> bytes:
        events = bytearray()
        # Optional tempo meta event
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            tempo_us_qn = rng.choice([500000, 400000, 600000, 750000, 300000])  # 120,150,100,80,200 bpm
            events += _varlen(0) + bytes([0xFF, 0x51, 0x03]) + tempo_us_qn.to_bytes(3, 'big')
        # Time signature meta (optional)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            nn = rng.choice([2,3,4,5,6,7])
            dd_pow = rng.choice([0,1,2,3])  # denominator as 2^dd
            met = 24
            thirtyseconds = 8
            events += _varlen(0) + bytes([0xFF, 0x58, 0x04, nn, dd_pow, met, thirtyseconds])
        # Key signature (optional)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sf = rng.randint(-7, 7) & 0xFF
            mi = rng.choice([0,1])
            events += _varlen(0) + bytes([0xFF, 0x59, 0x02, sf, mi])
        # Program change on channel 0
        prog = rng.randint(0, 127)
        events += _varlen(rng.randint(0, 10)) + bytes([0xC0, prog])
        # A few note on/off pairs to ensure audible content
        pitch_base = rng.randint(48, 72)
        for i in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            pitch = max(0, min(127, pitch_base + rng.randint(-5, 5)))
            vel_on = rng.randint(60, 110)
            vel_off = rng.randint(20, 80)
            dt_on = rng.randint(0, 60)
            dt_off = rng.randint(30, 240)
            events += _varlen(dt_on) + bytes([0x90, pitch, vel_on])
            events += _varlen(dt_off) + bytes([0x80, pitch, vel_off])
        # End of track
        events += _varlen(0) + bytes([0xFF, 0x2F, 0x00])
        return b"MTrk" + _u32be(len(events)) + bytes(events)

    tracks = b"".join(make_track() for _ in range(ntrks))
    return header + tracks


def _maybe_make_alt_format(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally emit a different valid format the library might accept
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        # MUS (Doom) header minimal stub with data; many decoders can handle MUS
        # Header: "MUS\x1A" + little-endian fields
        id_ = b"MUS\x1A"
        score_len = 32
        score_start = 16
        primary_channels = 9
        secondary_channels = 0
        instr_cnt = 0
        # Little endian helpers
        le16 = lambda v: v.to_bytes(2, 'little')
        header = id_ + le16(score_len) + le16(score_start) + le16(primary_channels) + le16(secondary_channels) + le16(instr_cnt)
        body = bytes([0x00, 0x60, 0x00, 0x60, 0x60, 0x00]) * 6 + b"\x0F"  # simplistic event stream
        return header + body
    elif choice < 0.5:
        # HMI/XMI are more involved; fallback to another valid MIDI
        return _make_simple_smf(rng)
    else:
        # Module formats are complex; produce a small WAV ensuring CreateDecoder paths valid
        # Minimal valid PCM WAV 44-byte header + a short sine-like buffer
        import math
        sr = rng.choice([22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
        ch = rng.choice([1, 2])
        bits = rng.choice([16])
        dur_s = rng.uniform(0.02, 0.2)
        n = max(1, int(sr * dur_s))
        freq = rng.choice([220, 440, 660])
        # PCM 16-bit little endian
        data = bytearray()
        for i in range(n * ch):
            t = (i // ch) / sr
            sample = int(32767 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * freq * t))
            data += sample.to_bytes(2, 'little', signed=True)
        datasz = len(data)
        fmt_chunk = (
            b"fmt " + (16).to_bytes(4, 'little') +
            (1).to_bytes(2, 'little') +  # PCM
            ch.to_bytes(2, 'little') +
            sr.to_bytes(4, 'little') +
            (sr * ch * bits // 8).to_bytes(4, 'little') +
            (ch * bits // 8).to_bytes(2, 'little') +
            bits.to_bytes(2, 'little')
        )
        data_chunk = b"data" + datasz.to_bytes(4, 'little') + bytes(data)
        riff_sz = 4 + (8 + len(fmt_chunk)) + (8 + len(data_chunk))
        wav = b"RIFF" + riff_sz.to_bytes(4, 'little') + b"WAVE" + fmt_chunk + data_chunk
        return wav


def _make_content_for_filename(rng: random.Random, filename: str) -> bytes:
    ext = os.path.splitext(filename)[1].lower().lstrip('.')
    if ext in ("mid", "midi", "xmi", "hmi", "mids"):
        return _make_simple_smf(rng)
    if ext == "mus":
        return _maybe_make_alt_format(rng)
    if ext in ("wav",):
        return _maybe_make_alt_format(rng)
    # For other extensions, provide a valid MIDI by default to drive the MIDI path
    return _make_simple_smf(rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a realistic path-like string. The harness will map this to an actual temp file.
    # Use a relative path with subdirectories to exercise path handling.
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(
            "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10))).strip()
        )
    filename = _rand_filename(rng)
    path = os.path.join(*parts, filename) if parts else filename

    content = _make_content_for_filename(rng, filename)

    # Package as: ASCII path string, NUL, then file content. The fuzzing framework that
    # provides FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME commonly writes our buffer to a temp file and returns
    # the path; embedding both path and content allows it to extract both.
    path_bytes = path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
    out = path_bytes + content
    return out[:4096]

def make_smf(r):
    # Standard MIDI File Type-1 with a single short track containing tempo and end-of-track.
    # Header: MThd, length 6, format 1, ntrks 1..3, division 480.
    fmt = 1
    ntrks = _rand(r, 1, 2)
    division = 480
    header = b"MThd" + struct.pack(
        ">IHHH", 6, fmt, ntrks, division
    )

    def varlen(val):
        # Encode variable length quantity
        out = []
        out.append(val & 0x7F)
        val >>= 7
        while val:
            out.append(0x80 | (val & 0x7F))
            val >>= 7
        return bytes(reversed(out))

    def make_track():
        events = []
        # Set tempo meta (120 BPM -> 500000 us/qn)
        tempo = _rand(r, 300000, 900000)
        events.append(varlen(0) + b"\xff\x51\x03" + struct.pack(
            ">I", tempo
        )[1:])
        # Program change ch0
        prog = _rand(r, 0, 127)
        events.append(varlen(0) + bytes([0xC0, prog]))
        # Note on/off pair
        note = _rand(r, 48, 72)
        vel = _rand(r, 60, 100)
        dur = _rand(r, 60, 240)
        events.append(varlen(0) + bytes([0x90, note, vel]))
        events.append(varlen(dur) + bytes([0x80, note, 0]))
        # End of track
        events.append(varlen(0) + b"\xff\x2f\x00")
        trk = b"".join(events)
        return b"MTrk" + struct.pack(">I", len(trk)) + trk

    tracks = b"".join(make_track() for _ in range(ntrks))
    blob = header + tracks
    return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]


def make_mus(r):
    # DOOM MUS minimal header + small payload. This is not a full sequence but passes header sniffers.
    # Header structure: "MUS\x1a", len 16+..., scoreLen, scoreStart, channels, secChannels, instrCnt, dummy[8]
    magic = b"MUS\x1a"
    # Minimal plausible fields
    score_len = 32
    score_start = 16
    channels = 4
    sec_channels = 0
    instr_cnt = 0
    header = magic + struct.pack(
        "<HHHHH", score_len, score_start, channels, sec_channels, instr_cnt
    ) + b"\x00" * 8
    # A couple of MUS events ending with 0x00 (end)
    payload = bytes([0x90, 0x00, 0x00]) + b"\x00"
    return (header + payload)[:_MAX_SIZE]


def make_hmi(r):
    # Minimal HMI header with zero/short sizes; heuristic detectors check magic.
    # HMI starts with "HMI-MIDISONG" + version etc.
    header = b"HMI-MIDISONG\x00"
    header += struct.pack("<HH", 0x0100, 0)  # version, numtracks
    header += _rand_bytes(r, 32)
    return header[:_MAX_SIZE]


def make_xmi(r):
    # XMI is IFF-like: FORM, CAT, XDIR. Provide minimal FORM XDIR.
    # This serves identification for detectors.
    form = b"FORM" + struct.pack(">I", 12) + b"XDIR" + b"INFO" + struct.pack(">I", 0)
    return form

def make_wav_pcm(r):

# --- Ogg Vorbis skeleton ---

def make_ogg_vorbis_min(r):
    # Minimal Ogg container with an identification header page; not a full stream but identifies as Ogg/Vorbis.
    def ogg_crc(packet):
        return zlib.crc32(packet) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    # Ogg page header fields
    capture = b"OggS"  # 0-3
    version = b"\x00"
    header_type = b"\x02"  # beginning of stream
    granule = b"\x00" * 8
    serial = struct.pack("<I", _rand(r, 1, 0xFFFFFFF0))
    seq = struct.pack("<I", 0)
    chk = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
    # Vorbis identification header packet
    vorb_id = b"\x01vorbis" + struct.pack("<I", 0)  # version 0
    ch = _rand(r, 1, 2)
    sr = random.choice([22050, 44100, 48000])
    vorb_id += bytes([ch]) + struct.pack("<I", sr) + b"\x00" * 4 * 4 + b"\x01\x20\x00\x00"
    segs = bytes([len(vorb_id)])
    head_wo_crc = capture + version + header_type + granule + serial + seq + chk + bytes([1]) + segs + vorb_id
    crc = struct.pack("<I", ogg_crc(head_wo_crc))
    page = (capture + version + header_type + granule + serial + seq + crc + bytes([1]) + segs + vorb_id)
    return page[:_MAX_SIZE]

def make_it(r):

# --- Simple compressed payload wrapped as DLS/SF2 hint (SF2 starts with RIFF...sfbk) ---

def make_sf2_hint(r):
    # RIFF sfbk container skeleton
    list_payload = _rand_bytes(r, 64)

_GENERATORS = [
    make_smf,
    make_mus,
    make_hmi,
    make_xmi,
    make_wav_pcm,
    make_ogg_vorbis_min,
    make_mod,
    make_s3m,

    make_xm,
    make_sf2_hint,
]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a primary format
    gen = r.choice(_GENERATORS)
    blob = gen(r)

    # Optionally append a small, valid metadata footer/header of another type that
    # some detectors parse for loop tags or embedded chunks, keeping size under limit.
    if len(blob) < _MAX_SIZE and r.random() < 0.35:
        tag_type = r.choice(["RIFFLIST", "ID3", "LOOPTAG"]) 
        extra = b""
        if tag_type == "RIFFLIST":
            # Append a small LIST chunk that some parsers ignore/scan for tags.
            payload = b"INFO" + _rand_bytes(r, _rand(r, 8, 24))
            extra = b"LIST" + struct.pack("<I", len(payload)) + payload
        elif tag_type == "ID3":
            # Simple ID3v2 header (not full MP3, but benign tag bytes)
            extra = b"ID3\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x10" + _rand_bytes(r, 16)
        else:
            # ASCII loop tags common in tracker/MIDI wrappers
            text = b"LOOPSTART=0\nLOOPEND=1000\n"
            extra = text
        keep = _MAX_SIZE - len(blob)
        blob += extra[:keep]

    return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for tagged audio data buffers that may include loop metadata.
# We craft several common container formats and tagging conventions:
# - RIFF/WAV with LIST/INFO IXML and smpl chunk (loop points)
# - Ogg Vorbis-style comments with LOOPSTART/LOOPEND
# - FLAC Vorbis comments
# - MP3 ID3v2 TXXX or COMM frames with LOOPSTART/LOOPEND
# - Plain text INI-like with loop tags
# - Minimal MIDI with text meta events containing loop tags
# - RAW with trailing tagged footer
# Keep sizes <= 4096 bytes and fields internally consistent.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _rand_u32(r):
    return r.randrange(0, 2**32)

def _pad2(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return data + (b"\x00" if (len(data) % 2) == 1 else b"")

# WAV helpers

def make_wav_with_smpl(r: random.Random, samplerate=44100, channels=2, bits=16,
                        loop_start=1000, loop_end=40000) -> bytes:
    # Build a tiny PCM WAV with fmt, smpl loop chunk, and minimal data.
    audio_frames = r.randint(64, 512)
    block_align = channels * (bits // 8)
    byte_rate = samplerate * block_align
    data_bytes = audio_frames * block_align

    fmt = struct.pack('<4sI4s', b'RIFF', 0, b'WAVE')
    fmt_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI', b'fmt ', 16)
    fmt_chunk += struct.pack('<HHIIHH', 1, channels, samplerate, byte_rate, block_align, bits)

    # smpl chunk according to spec, one loop
    manufacturer = 0
    product = 0
    sample_period = int(1e9 / samplerate)  # ns period
    midi_unity_note = 60
    pitch_fraction = 0
    smpte_format = 0
    smpte_offset = 0
    num_loops = 1
    sampler_data = 0
    smpl_header = struct.pack('<IIIIIIII', manufacturer, product, sample_period,
                              midi_unity_note, pitch_fraction, smpte_format,
                              smpte_offset, num_loops)
    smpl_header += struct.pack('<I', sampler_data)
    # loop struct: cueId, type(0 forward), start, end, fraction, playcount
    loop = struct.pack('<IIIIII', 0, 0, max(0, loop_start), max(loop_start, loop_end), 0, 0)
    smpl_data = smpl_header + loop
    smpl_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI', b'smpl', len(smpl_data)) + smpl_data

    # INFO LIST with textual LOOPSTART/LOOPEND as well
    list_payload = b''
    def info_tag(tag, val):
        b = val.encode('ascii')
        # tags are padded to even
        return struct.pack('<4sI', tag.encode('ascii'), len(b)) + _pad2(b)
    list_payload += info_tag('ICMT', f'Loop points LOOPSTART={loop_start} LOOPEND={loop_end}')
    list_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI4s', b'LIST', len(list_payload)+4, b'INFO') + list_payload

    # data chunk: fill with zeros
    data_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI', b'data', data_bytes) + (b'\x00' * data_bytes)

    body = _pad2(fmt_chunk) + _pad2(smpl_chunk) + _pad2(list_chunk) + _pad2(data_chunk)
    riff = fmt[:4] + struct.pack('<I', len(body)) + fmt[8:] + body
    return riff[:MAX_SIZE]


def make_wav_with_cue_labl(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create WAV with cue points and adtl labl text containing LOOP markers.
    samplerate = r.choice([22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    channels = r.choice([1, 2])
    bits = 16
    frames = r.randint(256, 2048)
    block_align = channels * (bits // 8)
    byte_rate = samplerate * block_align
    data_bytes = frames * block_align

    fmt_hdr = struct.pack('<4sI4s', b'RIFF', 0, b'WAVE')
    fmt_chunk = struct.pack('<4sIHHIIHH', b'fmt ', 16, 1, channels, samplerate, byte_rate, block_align, bits)

    # cue chunk: 2 points
    cue_points = []
    start_sample = r.randint(0, max(0, frames - 32))
    end_sample = r.randint(start_sample + 1, frames)
    cue_points.append((1, start_sample))
    cue_points.append((2, end_sample))
    cue_body = struct.pack('<I', len(cue_points))
    for cid, pos in cue_points:
        # id, position, dataChunkId, chunkStart, blockStart, sampleOffset
        cue_body += struct.pack('<IIIIII', cid, pos, 0x61746164, 0, 0, pos)  # 'data'
    cue_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI', b'cue ', len(cue_body)) + cue_body

    # adtl list with labels
    adtl = b''
    def labl(cid, text):
        tb = text.encode('ascii')
        entry = struct.pack('<4sI', b'labl', 4 + len(tb)) + struct.pack('<I', cid) + tb
        return _pad2(entry)
    adtl += labl(1, 'LOOPSTART')
    adtl += labl(2, 'LOOPEND')
    list_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI4s', b'LIST', len(adtl)+4, b'adtl') + adtl

    data_chunk = struct.pack('<4sI', b'data', data_bytes) + (b'\x00' * data_bytes)
    body = _pad2(fmt_chunk) + _pad2(cue_chunk) + _pad2(list_chunk) + _pad2(data_chunk)
    riff = fmt_hdr[:4] + struct.pack('<I', len(body)) + fmt_hdr[8:] + body
    return riff[:MAX_SIZE]

# Ogg Vorbis comments

def make_ogg_with_comments(r: random.Random, loop_start=10000, loop_end=120000) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal fake Ogg/Vorbis-like header pages with a comment packet containing loop tags.
    # Not a valid decodeable Ogg container, but typical parsers scan raw bytes for "LOOPSTART=..." in comments.
    header = b'OggS' + b'\x00' * 22
    id_hdr = b'\x01vorbis' + b'\x00' * 24

    vendor = b'gen\x00'
    comments = [
        f'LOOPSTART={loop_start}'.encode('ascii'),
        f'LOOPEND={loop_end}'.encode('ascii'),
        b'LOOPLENGTH=%d' % max(0, loop_end - loop_start),
    ]
    user_comments = b''
    user_comments += struct.pack('<I', len(comments))
    for c in comments:
        user_comments += struct.pack('<I', len(c)) + c
    comment_packet = b'\x03vorbis' + vendor + user_comments

    audio = b'\x00' * r.randint(256, 2048)
    blob = header + id_hdr + comment_packet + audio
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]

# FLAC Vorbis comment block

def make_flac_with_vorbis_comments(r: random.Random, ls=5000, le=90000) -> bytes:
    # FLAC stream marker + minimal METADATA_BLOCK_VORBIS_COMMENT
    flac = b'fLaC'
    vendor = b'gen'
    comments = [f'LOOPSTART={ls}'.encode('ascii'), f'LOOPEND={le}'.encode('ascii')]
    vc = struct.pack('<I', len(vendor)) + vendor
    vc += struct.pack('<I', len(comments))
    for c in comments:
        vc += struct.pack('<I', len(c)) + c
    is_last = 1
    block_type = 4  # VORBIS_COMMENT
    length = len(vc)
    header = struct.pack('>B', (is_last << 7) | block_type) + struct.pack('>I', length)[1:]
    blob = flac + header + vc + (b'\x00' * r.randint(64, 256))
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]

# MP3 with ID3v2 TXXX or COMM frames

def _id3v2_size(n):
    # synchsafe 28-bit
    b0 = (n >> 21) & 0x7F
    b1 = (n >> 14) & 0x7F
    b2 = (n >> 7) & 0x7F
    b3 = n & 0x7F
    return bytes([b0, b1, b2, b3])

def make_mp3_id3_loop(r: random.Random, ls=22050, le=441000) -> bytes:
    frames = []
    # TXXX frame: description LOOPSTART, value number
    def txxx(desc, val):
        enc = b'\x00'  # ISO-8859-1
        payload = enc + desc.encode('latin-1') + b'\x00' + str(val).encode('latin-1')
        size = len(payload)
        header = b'TXXX' + struct.pack('>I', size) + b'\x00\x00'
        return header + payload
    frames.append(txxx('LOOPSTART', ls))
    frames.append(txxx('LOOPEND', le))

    body = b''.join(frames)
    tag_size = len(body)
    id3 = b'ID3' + b'\x03\x00' + b'\x00' + _id3v2_size(tag_size) + body
    mp3_frames = b'\xff\xfb' + b'\x90\x64' + (b'\x00' * r.randint(64, 512))
    return (id3 + mp3_frames)[:MAX_SIZE]

# INI-like/plaintext

def make_ini_like(r: random.Random, ls=1000, le=90000) -> bytes:
    lines = []
    lines.append('[loop]')
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(f'LOOPSTART={ls}')
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(f'LOOPEND={le}')
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append(f'LOOPLENGTH={max(0, le-ls)}')
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append('comment=Intro section')
    text = '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
    return text.encode('utf-8')[:MAX_SIZE]

# Minimal MIDI with text meta events carrying tags

def make_midi_with_text_tags(r: random.Random, ls=0, le=48000) -> bytes:
    def chunk(idb, data):
        return idb + struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + data
    # Header MThd
    format_type = 0
    ntrks = 1
    division = 480  # PPQ
    mthd = chunk(b'MThd', struct.pack('>HHH', format_type, ntrks, division))

    # Track with meta text events at tick 0
    def varlen(n):
        out = []
        buffer = n & 0x7F
        while True:
            n >>= 7
            if n:
                buffer <<= 8
                buffer |= ((n & 0x7F) | 0x80)
            else:
                break
        while True:
            out.append(buffer & 0xFF)
            if buffer & 0x80:
                buffer >>= 8
            else:
                break
        return bytes(out)

    events = []
    def meta_text(text):
        return b'\x00' + b'\xff\x01' + bytes([len(text)]) + text
    events.append(meta_text(f'LOOPSTART={ls}'.encode('ascii')))
    events.append(meta_text(f'LOOPEND={le}'.encode('ascii')))
    # End of track
    events.append(b'\x00\xff\x2f\x00')

    mtrk_data = b''.join(events)
    mtrk = chunk(b'MTrk', mtrk_data)
    midi = mthd + mtrk
    return midi[:MAX_SIZE]

# RAW blob with footer tags

def make_raw_with_footer(r: random.Random, ls=4096, le=65536) -> bytes:
    payload = r.randbytes(r.randint(64, 512)) if hasattr(r, 'randbytes') else bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(r.randint(64, 512)))
    footer = (f'\n# LOOPSTART={ls}\n# LOOPEND={le}\n').encode('ascii')
    return (payload + footer)[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose loop points with sane ordering and positive values
    ls = r.randint(0, 200000)
    le = r.randint(ls + 1, ls + r.randint(100, 200000))

    builders = [
        lambda: make_wav_with_smpl(r, samplerate=r.choice([22050, 32000, 44100, 48000]),
                                   channels=r.choice([1, 2]), bits=16,
                                   loop_start=ls, loop_end=le),
        lambda: make_wav_with_cue_labl(r),
        lambda: make_ogg_with_comments(r, loop_start=ls, loop_end=le),
        lambda: make_flac_with_vorbis_comments(r, ls=ls, le=le),
        lambda: make_mp3_id3_loop(r, ls=ls, le=le),
        lambda: make_ini_like(r, ls=ls, le=le),
        lambda: make_midi_with_text_tags(r, ls=ls, le=le),
        lambda: make_raw_with_footer(r, ls=ls, le=le),
    ]

    # Bias towards WAV and Ogg which often contain loop tags
    weights = [3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1]
    choice_idx = r.choices(range(len(builders)), weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    blob = builders[choice_idx]()

    # Ensure not empty and within size
    if not blob:
        blob = make_ini_like(r, ls=ls, le=le)
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]
